name: Sunekos

lead: Sunekos is an injectable that combines hyaluronic acid with amino acids, offered in clinics for photoaged face skin, the eye area and lax skin on the thighs, knees and arms. People use it for firmer, less crepey skin.

The idea is that the amino acids supply building blocks for collagen and elastin and support fibroblast activity, so skin tissue is stimulated. Published work includes a multicenter cellulite study of 46 women, and registered small studies cover the face, under-eyes and body.

paras: A clinician injects the mixture into or beneath the dermis at several points over the area being treated, typically across a short course of sessions. It is used on the face, around the eyes and on body skin.
The cellulite study assessed safety alongside efficacy. As with other injectables, local swelling and bruising are expected, and long-term safety data are limited.

angle.text: Sunekos is an Italian biorevitalising booster that combines hyaluronic acid and amino acids, used for firmer skin on photoaged faces, around the eyes and on lax areas like the thighs and arms. The amino acids are meant to supply building blocks for collagen and elastin. Support is mainly small manufacturer-linked trials.

lead: Sunekos is a commercially available injectable made of hyaluronic acid and amino acids in an alkaline solution, used in aesthetic clinics as a skin 'biorevitalising' treatment.[1] People have it to improve skin quality and firmness: practitioners and the maker present it for facial photoaging, the area around the eyes, and skin laxity or cellulite on the body.[2][3][4][5][6]

The brand is made by Sunekos Laboratories, which lists Professional Dietetics S.p.A. of Milan, Italy, as its company. Its site describes the products as nourishing the skin with amino acids and lists an injectable line that includes Sunekos 200, Performa, 1200, Body and Cell 15, marketed respectively for general skin renovation, body laxity and stretch marks, and cellulite.[6]

Published human research is limited to a handful of studies. A 2026 prospective multicenter study evaluated the mixture for cellulite (edematous fibrosclerotic panniculopathy) in 46 women, reporting on efficacy and safety, and several small registered studies cover the face, under-eyes and body.[1][2][3][4][5]

paras: The product combines hyaluronic acid, a hydrating molecule found in skin, with a blend of amino acids in an alkaline solution.[1][6] The maker's site describes variants for different needs, including an enhanced formula called Performa for skin renovation, Sunekos Body for stretch marks and laxity, and Sunekos Cell 15 for cellulite.[6] The site gives no further composition details and lists awards rather than regulatory approvals.[6]

The treatment is delivered by a clinician as a series of injections placed in or just beneath the skin. In the 2026 cellulite investigation, severity was scored before the first, second and third injection sessions and again at 3 and 6 months after treatment started.[1] A registered half-face study compared an interstitial or 'cushion' technique with a bolus technique at five points per side for photoaging.[2]

Proponents say the amino acids supply building blocks for collagen and elastin and support fibroblast activity, while hyaluronic acid contributes hydration; the maker's materials describe products acting 'in a physiological way'.[6] The published studies located assess clinical appearance rather than testing this mechanism directly.[1]

The 2026 cellulite study was prospective and multicenter and enrolled 46 women with stage I to early stage IV disease. Improvement was rated by clinicians and patients on modified photonumeric cellulite severity scales, and the psychological impact of cellulite was also measured; the study also assessed safety.[1] The authors note that cellulite affects roughly 80 to 98 percent of postpubertal women and that its multifactorial origin makes management difficult.[1]

Registered studies include a twelve-person half-face comparison of two injection techniques for photoaging,[2] a 25-person intradermal photoaging study,[5] a 22-person under-eye dark circle study,[4] and a 24-person study on inner thighs, knees and arms.[3] All are listed as completed; posted results were not available.

The cellulite study assessed safety alongside efficacy.[1] As with other skin injectables, local reactions at injection sites such as swelling and bruising are generally expected; long-term safety data specific to this product are limited.

Sunekos is marketed to clinics as part of the 'skin booster' category and promoted through industry awards; the maker reports a 2023 Medical Beauty Awards honour for Performa and further awards in 2025.[6] It appears mainly in clinic and practitioner communications rather than in looksmaxxing forum discussion.
